title: sessions: stop synced customization bundle churn restarting agent host sessions
body:
## Problem

The synthetic **"VS Code Synced Data"** plugin (`vscode-synced-customization:/<sessionType>`) is a **single window-global artifact shared by every session** of a session type, identified by a content-hash `nonce`.

It was being built partly from **workspace-scoped** inputs:
- `PromptsStorage.local` files (`.github/instructions`, `.github/skills`, `.github/agents`, `.github/prompts`)
- workspace-discovered MCP servers (`.vscode/mcp.json`, folder-root `.mcp.json`)

In the Agents window the workspace is **not stable**: `WorkspaceFolderManagementContribution` rewrites workspace folder 0 to follow the active session. Relative locations like `.github/instructions` are resolved against workspace folder roots (`PromptFilesLocator.toAbsoluteLocations`), so the *same* bundle path is filled with a *different worktree's* bytes depending on which session is focused.

## How that turns into a hung session

The nonce churn alone isn't the failure. `requiresRestart` is only ever evaluated on **send** (`_sendMessage`), against the snapshot captured when the session was last **resumed**. The hang comes from a race between those two moments. Full trace of one occurrence:

```
21:27:43.136  activeClientSet arrives, nonce = -529975129   ← STALE (previous worktree)
21:27:43.182  _resumeSession — session not in memory, resuming...
                 └─ appliedSnapshot captured = -529975129
21:27:46.330  Restored session with 29 turns
21:27:54.197  activeClientSet arrives, nonce = 1461338636   ← settled to THIS session's worktree
21:27:54.220  sendMessage: cachedEntry=true
21:27:54.220  Session configuration changed, refreshing session   ← -529975129 != 1461338636
21:27:54.522  No cached entry (was evicted by requiresRestart), calling _resumeSession
```

Clicking a session resumes it **immediately**, snapshotting the bundle while it still reflects the *previous* session's worktree. The bundle settles to the correct worktree seconds later. Sending inside that window destroys and resumes the same SDK session id, which trips a race in the Copilot runtime (`@github/copilot@1.0.79-2`) that silently orphans the session: `session.send()` returns normally, but the prompt is never persisted, no model turn starts, and no error is emitted — the UI spins forever.

Note `1461338636` is exactly the nonce this session had the last time it was focused: returning to a session *does* re-resolve identically. The restart happens because the snapshot was taken mid-switch, not because the steady states differ.

The runtime race is being fixed separately; this PR removes the trigger.

## Evidence

Reconstructed every bundle from a live 85-minute `agenthost.log` + AHP transport log (one Agents window, many worktrees) and diffed consecutive bundles. Of 50 transitions from a single client:

| Cause of bundle change | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Content of `skills/sessions/SKILL.md` / `rules/buildNext.instructions.md` — same path, **different worktree** | 30 |
| `.mcp.json` only — `${workspaceFolder}` `cwd` flipping between worktrees | 10 |
| File-set change (incl. a skill renamed on one branch only) | 5 |
| No observable change | 5 |

- `.mcp.json`'s resolved `cwd` took **17 distinct worktree paths** across 51 scans.
- Only **one** client churned (23 distinct nonces). The other four emitted exactly **one** each — regular windows have stable workspaces.
- Every session that got refreshed had seen **2–6 distinct nonces** shortly beforehand: sessions receive nonces derived from *other* worktrees, because the bundle is global.
- 37 refresh events across the two log files.

This was also a **correctness** bug: sessions received `coding-guidelines.instructions.md` from their own worktree via native per-session discovery **plus a stale second copy from an unrelated worktree** via the bundle.

## Fix

Exclude workspace-scoped content from the window-global bundle where the workspace is session-derived, via a new `ILocalCustomizationSyncOptions.includeWorkspaceStorage`. With the bundle no longer a function of the workspace, it is constant — so the resume-time and send-time values are always equal and the race window disappears.

Every caller states the value explicitly, because the right answer depends on facts the service cannot see:

- **local agent host** (runs in both window types) → `!isSessionsWindow`. `SessionCustomizationDiscovery` already reads `.github/instructions|skills|agents|hooks` from **each session's own working directory**, which is the correct per-session source.
- **remote agent host** → `true`. The host is on another machine and cannot discover any of this client's files, so the bundle is load-bearing rather than redundant — the same reason it opts into user storage.

Also fixes a latent collision in `AgentPluginManager`: nonces are signed 32-bit hashes and `_sanitize` stripped the sign, so `-N` and `N` mapped to the **same directory** while being tracked as **distinct LRU entries** — evicting one deleted the other's materialized content.

## Before / after

Replaying the 49 recorded bundle scans through the new logic:

```
BEFORE (as shipped):  distinct bundles = 20   re-syncs = 44
AFTER  (with fix):    distinct bundles =  1   re-syncs =  0
```

## Tradeoff reviewers should weigh

Workspace `.github/prompts` (bundled as `commands/`) is the **only** synced type with no native per-session discovery, so those slash commands no longer reach Agents-window sessions.

I judged a slash command from an unrelated worktree to be worse than none, and skills are the supported replacement for prompt files on agent-host harnesses. But it is a visible reduction and it is a one-line predicate if we disagree.

## Known limitation this exposes

The bundle URI is `vscode-synced-customization:/<sessionType>` — **identical across windows** — while each window builds its own content, and `SessionPluginController` dedupes client customizations by URI (first client wins). Two windows attached to the same session can therefore publish the same URI with different nonces, and the winner depends on client insertion order. This change reduces the exposure (the Agents-window bundle becomes a function of machine-global state) but does not remove it.

The real fix for both this and the `.github/prompts` gap is **bundling per session rather than per window**, which would also close the resume/send race by construction. Out of scope here.

## Considered and rejected

Loosening `requiresRestart` / `parsedPluginsEqual` to compare semantic content instead of nonce-derived URIs. Since the nonce *is* a content hash, that comparison is already equivalent to comparing content — and the trace shows it behaved correctly: the two values genuinely differed because one was computed from the wrong worktree. Loosening it would only mask the bug and stop sessions picking up genuine instruction edits.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — clean
- Targeted unit tests: 393 passing (chat agentSessions + `agentPluginManager`), 54 passing (remote provider)
- New tests cover the workspace-exclusion behaviour and the negative-nonce directory collision; the nonce regression test was verified to **fail without** the fix.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Use $XDG_STATE_HOME for `APPLICATION_SHARED` storage (`~/.<app>-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb`)

labels.name: debt
labels.description: Code quality issues

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Work not yet planned for a specific release.

body:
## Current limitation

PR #311317 introduced `StorageScope.APPLICATION_SHARED`, storing shared state at `~/.<app>-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb` (e.g. `~/.vscode-shared/`, `~/.vscode-insiders-shared/`). The path is hardcoded under `$HOME` with no `$XDG_STATE_HOME` resolution. This is configurable via `--shared-data-dir`, but the **default** clutters `$HOME` and violates the [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/latest/).

## Desired improvement

Default the `appSharedDataHome` path to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/<app>-shared/` instead of `~/<app>-shared/`, with a one-time migration of the existing database and a fallback read of the old path for compatibility.

Per the XDG spec v0.8 (May 2021), `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `~/.local/state`) is the correct category for this data:

> The `$XDG_STATE_HOME` contains state data that should persist between (application) restarts, but that is not important or portable enough to the user that it should be stored in `$XDG_DATA_HOME`. It may contain:
> - actions history (logs, history, recently used files, …)
> - current state of the application that can be reused on a restart (view, layout, open files, undo history, …)

The contents of `state.vscdb` (`history.recentlyOpenedPathsList`, workspace trust markers, storage markers) match this definition exactly — it is restart-persisting, non-portable state, not user data or config.

## Workflow example

```bash
# Before (current):
#   ~/.vscode-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb
#   ~/.vscode-insiders-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb

# After (XDG-compliant default):
$XDG_STATE_HOME=/home/user/.local/state
#   ~/.local/state/vscode-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb
#   ~/.local/state/vscode-insiders-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb

# --shared-data-dir still overrides for users who need a custom path
```

## Impact and context

This is a long-standing XDG compliance gap (see #3884, #162712, #84808, #100988, #126182, #132971). PR #311317 added a **new** hardcoded `~/` path despite community requests in the PR comments to use `~/.local/state/`. Each new `~/.*-shared/` directory perpetuates the problem.

Because `APPLICATION_SHARED` is a **platform-level** feature in VS Code's storage layer (`IEnvironmentService.appSharedDataHome`), every VS Code-derived Electron app inherits this path. The top 5 clones that would benefit from an upstream fix:

| App | Vendor | Inherited path |
|-----|--------|---------------|
| **Cursor** | Anysphere | `~/.cursor-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb` |
| **Windsurf / Devin Desktop** | Cognition | `~/.windsurf-shared/`, `~/.devin-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb` |
| **Antigravity** | Google | `~/.antigravity-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb` |
| **VSCodium** | Community | `~/.vscodium-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb` |
| **Trae** | ByteDance | `~/.trae-shared/sharedStorage/state.vscdb` |

Fixing this in VS Code's `appSharedDataLocation` resolution (in `environmentService.ts`) benefits the entire ecosystem without each fork needing to patch the platform independently.

## Related

- #3884 — umbrella issue: "Revisit VS Code folder structure for app data, settings, extensions" (open since 2016)
- #162712 — "Support `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for the `argv.json` file"
- #311317 — PR that introduced `APPLICATION_SHARED` storage scope (merged, comments request XDG compliance)
- #311337 — original issue for cross-app state sharing

title: Terminal: expose xterm.js `mouseEventsRequireAlt` as a setting so mouse reporting never costs text selection
body:
<!-- Type: Feature Request. Repo: microsoft/vscode -->

### Problem

When a TUI application enables mouse reporting (`CSI ? 1000 h` and friends), the integrated terminal stops creating selections: `mousedown` is forwarded to the application instead. That is correct behaviour, but it means a single application choice silently removes the user's ability to select and copy text with the mouse — with no setting to opt out.

This is increasingly common: full-screen TUIs (Claude Code, various agents and TUI editors) arm mouse tracking by default, and users discover the terminal "can no longer select text" without any way to relate it to the application.

`Shift`+drag is a workaround, but it is undiscoverable and it is not what people reach for.

### Proposal

xterm.js already implements exactly the arbitration needed, in `SelectionService.shouldForceSelection()` / the `mouseEventsRequireAlt` option: when it is enabled, mouse reporting stays armed but only takes the click while the modifier is held, so plain drags keep selecting.

The option is present in the `@xterm/xterm` build VS Code ships, but it is never set — I could not find a single reference to `mouseEventsRequireAlt` anywhere in the shipped `out/` tree, so it stays at its default (`false`).

Exposing it would be a small, local change:

```jsonc
// proposed
"terminal.integrated.mouseEventsRequireModifier": false  // default: today's behaviour
```

When `true`, pass `mouseEventsRequireAlt: true` to the `Terminal` constructor / `options`. Users who prefer selection over in-app clicking flip one setting, once, and it applies to every TUI they run — instead of chasing a per-application environment variable each time.

### Why a setting rather than per-application handling

The terminal is the only layer that can arbitrate this: applications legitimately want mouse events, and users legitimately want selection. Today the application wins unconditionally and the user has no vote.

### Extra context for the browser case (code-server)

In `code-server` the impact is larger than on the desktop: the standard copy paths already go through an async IPC hop that breaks the clipboard user-gesture, so users end up relying on the browser's native DOM selection — which is precisely what disappears when mouse reporting is armed. Losing the selection there removes the last working copy path to the OS clipboard.

### Environment

- VS Code 1.131.0 as bundled by code-server 4.131.0, xterm.js `@xterm/xterm` 6.1.0-beta.291
- Verified with the shipped bundle loaded standalone and driven with real mouse events: with no tracking a plain drag selects; with `?1000h ?1006h` or the full set it selects nothing; `Shift`+drag selects in every case.

title: Let piece tree's nodeAt and nodeAt2 return null
body:
Fixes #228362

`nodeAt` and `nodeAt2` can both fall out of their search loops and end with `return null!`, so every caller was typed as receiving a `NodePosition` while actually being handed `null`.

This is not hypothetical. `findMatchesLineByLine` already guards with explicit `=== null` checks, which the current types make look like unreachable code:

```ts
let startPosition = this.nodeAt2(searchRange.startLineNumber, searchRange.startColumn);
if (startPosition === null) {
    return [];
}
```

This changes the return type to `NodePosition | null` and handles it at each of the call sites.

### Read paths

Chosen to match what the surrounding code already does for the equivalent "nothing there" case:

| Call site | Behaviour when `null` |
| --- | --- |
| `getCharCode`, `getLineCharCode` | return `0`, which is what `_getCharCode` already returns when there is no adjacent node |
| `getValueInRange`, `getNearestChunk` | return the empty string |
| `equal` | report the buffers as different — a missing node means the other buffer ended early |
| `findMatchesLineByLine` | return the matches collected so far |

### Mutation paths

`insert` and `delete` use `assertReturnsDefined` rather than a graceful fallback. Silently skipping a mutation would leave the piece tree out of sync with the model, which is worse than failing, so these keep throwing — just with a meaningful error instead of a property access on `null`.

### Risk

Every one of these sites previously dereferenced `null` and threw a `TypeError`, so behaviour is unchanged whenever a node is found, which is to say in all normal operation. The change only affects what happens on a path that already crashed.

### Verification

I reviewed the types by hand and did not run a local compile or the piece tree test suite, so please let CI be the judge. The existing `pieceTreeTextBuffer` tests cover these methods heavily and should exercise the read paths.

title: Fix terminal prompt duplication when resizing the terminal panel
body:
Fixes #329946 (partial — see "Known limitations" below)

## Summary

When the terminal panel is resized, the shell prompt can be duplicated / new prompt lines created on every resize instead of the buffer reflowing cleanly. Two causes in the terminal resize path:

1. **Redundant PTY resizes on every layout event.** `TerminalResizeDebouncer.resize()` fired a resize even when the grid dimensions did not change (e.g. while dragging the panel), sending a PTY resize (SIGWINCH) on every layout event. Shells repaint the prompt on SIGWINCH, so this produced a storm of prompt redraws while dragging.

2. **Horizontal resizes debounced too briefly.** The debounced horizontal resize fired after 100ms, but shells such as zsh need longer than that to fully process a prompt redraw after a resize. When resizes arrived back-to-back, the shell computed its prompt redraw from a stale terminal width, which misplaces the erase/rewrite and leaves duplicated prompt fragments in the buffer.

## Changes

`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalResizeDebouncer.ts`:
- Skip the resize entirely (and cancel any pending debounced resize) when the requested `cols`/`rows` equal the current grid — no more redundant PTY resizes / SIGWINCH storms while dragging.
- Only fire the immediate Y-resize when `rows` actually changed, and only schedule the debounced X-resize when `cols` actually changed.
- Increase `DebounceResizeXDelay` from 100ms to 300ms so the shell's prompt redraw is fully processed between consecutive resizes.

## Verification

- Reproduced the duplication headlessly with a real zsh 5.9 and bash shell in a pty driving the bundled xterm.js: with the 100ms debounce the buffer ended with 3 prompt copies after a shrink/grow/shrink cycle; with 300ms exactly 1 copy.
- Verified in a running Code OSS instance (launched with playwright over CDP): resizing the bottom-panel terminal (long prompt, shrink/grow cycles, continuous drags) reflows cleanly with no duplication.

## Known limitations (honest assessment)

This fixes the common cases (panel resizing at moderate widths, continuous drags). It does **not** fix every duplication scenario:

- **Extreme-narrow terminals with colored prompts** (e.g. terminal docked in the side panel and shrunk to its minimum width, ~15-20 columns, with a colored `PS1`/`PROMPT`): the prompt can still duplicate. Root cause: xterm.js deliberately does not reflow the cursor line on non-Windows (`reflowCursorLine=false`), so the prompt is a single buffer row rendered wrapped across several visual rows. The shell's redraw (readline/zsh) operates on visual rows, so its erase/rewrite misses rows and fragments accumulate. Enabling `reflowCursorLine` makes this worse due to https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5295 (cursor mispositioned on reflow of cursor line), which the xterm.js maintainers have declined to fix. Upstream VS Code has no fix for this either; it would require a change in xterm.js or readline.

title: chat: preserve streamed response text when tool_calls delta is empty
body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329963

- Streamed assistant text is no longer dropped when a chat-completions response attaches an empty `tool_calls: []` array to content chunks.
- Fixes Custom Endpoint / BYOK models (for example vLLM-backed) where the model answered correctly and was billed, but the chat showed "Sorry, no response was returned".
- Scope is limited to the streaming chat-completions parser. The Responses API, Anthropic Messages API, and non-streaming paths are unaffected.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

`SSEProcessor` routed each streamed delta through a chain of mutually exclusive branches gated by a shared `handled` flag. The first branch tested `if (choice.delta?.tool_calls)`, which only checks truthiness. An empty array is truthy, so a delta like `{"content":" I","tool_calls":[]}` entered the tool-call branch, iterated zero tool calls, and left `handled` set to `true`. That skipped the terminal `if (!handled) { solution.append(choice); … }` path — the only place `delta.content` is read — so the visible text was discarded. Backends that attach `tool_calls: []` to every content delta (observed with vLLM 0.22.1) therefore lost the entire response, chunk by chunk, while the stream still finished with `stop` and tokens were still counted.

### Implementation

Guard the branch on `choice.delta?.tool_calls?.length` so an empty array is treated as "no tool calls" and falls through to normal content handling. This mirrors how OpenAI-compatible streaming clients handle the same payload: they iterate `tool_calls` and no-op on an empty array instead of gating the content path on its mere presence.

### Behavior and constraints

- Non-empty tool-call streaming (begin-tool-call emission, argument accumulation, finish handling) is unchanged.
- Empty `tool_calls: []` deltas now behave exactly like a plain content delta.
- Out of scope: a delta that carries visible text together with a non-empty `tool_calls` array in the same chunk. That is a rarer backend behavior and is intentionally not addressed by this minimal fix.
- Only the streaming chat-completions processor is touched; Responses, Messages, and non-streaming response processors use separate paths.

### Review context

- Fixes #329963.
- A focused regression test drives content deltas carrying `tool_calls: []` through to a `stop` completion and asserts the text survives.

</details>

title: Use modifier from mouse event in editor drag and drop
body:
Fixes #58515

In the discussion linked from that issue, @alexdima suggested reading the modifier state off the mouse event in `_onEditorMouseDrop` rather than tracking it across keydown/keyup. This does that and drops the `_modifierPressed` field.

### The tracked flag also looks buggy

`onEditorKeyUp` guarded its reset with `hasTriggerModifier(e)`:

```ts
if (hasTriggerModifier(e)) {
    this._modifierPressed = false;
}
```

On the keyup of Alt/Ctrl itself, that modifier already reads as released, so `hasTriggerModifier(e)` is `false` and the reset never runs. `_modifierPressed` stayed `true` from the first modifier press until the editor lost focus. Since `_onEditorMouseDrop` OR-ed it into the copy decision, a later plain drag and drop should have copied the selection instead of moving it. Reading the drop event's own modifier makes that state unrepresentable.

I want to be upfront that I reasoned this out from the code and browser modifier semantics rather than reproducing it in a running build, so treat the bug part as expected-not-observed.

### What I deliberately kept

The issue thread suggested also removing `onEditorKeyDown`/`onEditorKeyUp`, `_onEditorMouseDown`/`_onEditorMouseUp` and `_mouseDown`. I left those in place:

- The key handlers still do real work — they update `mouseStyle` to `copy`/`default` mid-drag. `_onEditorMouseDrag` only fires while the mouse is *moving*, so pressing the modifier while holding the mouse still would leave a stale cursor.
- `_mouseDown` is what stops those handlers from flipping the cursor to `copy` when the modifier is tapped with no drag in progress.
- `_onEditorMouseUp` resets `mouseStyle` to `text`, which is behavior rather than bookkeeping.

Happy to remove them too if you consider that cursor case not worth keeping.

### Verification

`tsc --noEmit -p src/tsconfig.json` and `eslint` on the changed file both pass. There is no existing test coverage for editor drag and drop that I could find, so nothing to extend there.

body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf215eed-072e-40bb-925d-f5149b6e5896

## Summary

- add a first-stage command-vs-chat intent decision to omni-chat routing
- restrict command routing to a curated set of reversible built-in VS Code UI commands
- shortlist and classify commands using localized command titles only; command IDs are never sent to the model
- deterministically recognize common directives such as `toggle terminal`, `toggle panel`, and `change VS Code theme`

- use a 5-second session-routing countdown, retaining 10 seconds for multi-root workspaces where folder selection may require more time

## Commands eligible for execution

Only the following currently enabled built-in commands are considered. All other built-in and extension commands continue through chat/session routing.

title: Show folder picker for Omni new sessions
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84913ee3-412a-4a1b-aea7-6ce01e6f1ac4

## Description

Omni already computed a workspace folder for new sessions, but its common new-session paths dispatched immediately. In multi-root workspaces this bypassed the destination panel, so users saw neither the selected folder nor a way to correct it before dispatch.

## Folder routing

For a new session in a multi-root workspace, Omni chooses the folder in this order:

1. **Explicit folder mention:** matches the prompt against a workspace folder's display name or final path segment. Matching is case-insensitive, treats spaces, dots, underscores, and hyphens equivalently, recognizes “VS Code” as “vscode”, ignores names shorter than three characters, and prefers the longest match.
2. **Attached resource:** uses the workspace folder containing the first attached file or resource that maps into the workspace.
3. **Related session:** uses the first model-ranked result with confidence of at least 0.35 whose working directory or repository metadata maps to a workspace folder. Working directory is checked before repository path, and nested matches prefer the deepest folder.
4. **Default folder:** uses the last folder selected for a new Agent Host session when it is still part of the workspace.
5. **Final fallback:** uses the first workspace folder.

The inferred destination is displayed as **New session in _folder_**. Its compact folder control opens an Agents-style searchable workspace menu anchored inside Omni. The menu lists every current workspace root with its full path and selected state, plus **Choose Folder…** for the native folder dialog and standalone working directories. Opening either picker pauses the countdown and closing or selecting resumes from the remaining time.

Standalone folders use the existing Agent Host trust boundary: before spawning, workspace roots request workspace trust and external folders request resource trust for the selected URI. Declining aborts the agent invocation.

The model picker renders in an adjacent transparent host above Omni, while the folder picker renders in a detached host to Omni's right. Neither picker resizes Omni. Omni's temporary local compose session also explicitly uses the Copilot Agent Host model pool, so the model picker shows the available targeted models instead of only **Auto**.

## Changes

- Route multi-root new sessions through the correctable destination panel.
- Show the inferred folder in a compact folder/chevron control before dispatch.
- List all workspace roots in an anchored, searchable, accessible folder menu.
- Add an Agents-style **Choose Folder…** action backed by the native folder dialog.
- Preserve the existing Agent Host workspace/resource trust gate for selected folders.
- Keep the model picker detached above Omni and open the folder picker to its right without resizing Omni.
- Use the Agent Host model pool for Omni's routing composer.
- Preserve automatic dispatch with the existing 10-second countdown and pause/resume behavior.
- Keep single-root new sessions on the immediate path.
- Add browser coverage for explicit folder inference, workspace selection, native folder selection, anchoring, filtering, and countdown behavior.

Fixes #329698

title: Agent Host DEP0169 warning breaks product sanity matrix across Stable and Insiders

labels.name: important
labels.description: Issue identified as high-priority

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
## Impact

The 1.133 Stable product build and both scheduled Insider product builds are partially succeeding because **18 sanity-test matrix jobs fail deterministically**. This affects the published-product validation matrix across Linux distributions and architectures, macOS arm64, and Windows x64/arm64.

This should be treated as important for 1.133 because it leaves the release without passing sanity coverage on most supported platforms.

## Affected builds

- Stable: [463132 / 20260810.12](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=463132) — `release/1.133`, commit `4bef75520b2f8d1d76a1e44962dbada7a7b34a7b`, partially succeeded
- Scheduled Insider: [463088 / 20260810.7](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=463088) — `main`, commit `5a36a9c68ce6300f94225aff5f8db533671af98b`, partially succeeded
- Scheduled Insider: [463163 / 20260810.18](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=463163) — `main`, commit `038d70cd7962a7ac397477b33234058894256612`, partially succeeded

The ordinary successful Insider CI builds are not counterexamples: they run unit/browser/remote tests but do not run the published-product sanity matrix. The scheduled Insider product builds do run it and reproduce this failure.

## Failure

Every failed matrix leg reaches the same `server-web-*` failure:

```text
Test failed with error: [Server] [IPC Library: Agent Host] (node:1234) [DEP0169] DeprecationWarning: `url.parse()` behavior is not standardized and prone to errors that have security implications. Use the WHATWG URL API instead. CVEs are not issued for `url.parse()` vulnerabilities.
```

Mocha then reports:

```text
1) server-web-linux-x64
Error: [Server] [IPC Library: Agent Host] (node:...) [DEP0169] DeprecationWarning: `url.parse()` behavior is not standardized...
    at Socket.<anonymous> (.../test/sanity/out/context.js:1298:32)

Mocha test run finished: 1 failure(s)
```

## Failing matrix pattern

In build 463132, the failures are:

- Fedora 42 arm64 and amd64
- Fedora 43 arm64 and amd64
- CentOS Stream 9 arm64 and amd64
- openSUSE Leap 16.0 arm64 and amd64
- Alpine 3.22 arm64 and amd64
- Debian 11 arm64 and amd64
- Debian 12 arm64 and amd64
- Ubuntu 22.04 x64 Native
- macOS arm64
- Windows arm64 and x64

The passing jobs either do not have the `browser` capability or otherwise do not execute the `server-web-*` sanity case. For example, Debian 11 amd64 has `Capabilities: linux, x64, deb, desktop, browser, github-account` and fails `server-web-linux-x64`, while Ubuntu 22.04 amd64 lacks the `browser` capability and passes.

## Root cause analysis

PR #329706 (`5fb9376dbdc8b0f1bdc9eb8186f429e023503f92`, **agentHost: run the agent host on the remote server**) introduced the behavior that exposes the existing deprecated parse call during server-web sanity testing.

The sequence is:

1. A browser-capable sanity job starts a published `server-*-web` build.
2. The renderer connects to the remote server.
3. The remote server's new default Agent Host path registers a lazy `agentHostProxy` channel and starts a local Agent Host on first renderer connection.
4. The Agent Host WebSocket server validates its connection token using `url.parse()` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/webSocketTransport.ts`:

   ```ts
   const parsedUrl = url.parse(info.req.url ?? '', true);
   const token = parsedUrl.query[connectionTokenQueryName];
   ```

5. Node emits `[DEP0169] DeprecationWarning` to the Agent Host stderr.
6. The server forwards/prefixes that child stderr as:

   ```text
   [Server] [IPC Library: Agent Host] (node:...) [DEP0169] DeprecationWarning: ...
   ```

7. `test/sanity/src/context.ts` deliberately treats Node warnings as non-fatal, but its `isNonFatalCliStderr()` expression permits only one bracketed logging prefix before `(node:...)`:

   ```ts
   /(^|\n)(?:\[[^\]]+\]\s*)?(?:\(node:\d+\)\s*)?(?:\[[A-Z0-9]+\]\s*)?(?:[A-Za-z]+Warning|Warning):/
   ```

   It therefore does not match the two prefixes `[Server] [IPC Library: Agent Host]` and `runCliApp()` rejects the stderr chunk as a fatal test error.

This explains why the warning could exist without failing previous sanity runs: #329706 made the remote server start Agent Host during `server-web-*`, and the extra Agent Host logger prefix falls outside the harness's intended non-fatal-warning pattern.

## Suggested fix

The root fix is to stop generating the warning:

- Replace `url.parse()` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/webSocketTransport.ts` with the WHATWG `URL` API while preserving query-token behavior.

The sanity harness should also be hardened so its existing policy of treating deprecation warnings as non-fatal survives nested component prefixes:

- Update `isNonFatalCliStderr()` in `test/sanity/src/context.ts` to accept repeated structured prefixes before the Node warning.
- Add focused coverage for a message shaped like:

  ```text
  [Server] [IPC Library: Agent Host] (node:1234) [DEP0169] DeprecationWarning: ...
  ```

## Validation

Re-run a product build or focused sanity validation covering at least:

- one Linux job with the `browser` capability and `server-web-linux-x64`
- Windows x64 or arm64 `server-web-win32-*`
- macOS arm64 `server-web-darwin-arm64`

Expected result: Agent Host starts and connects without emitting `DEP0169`, and all browser-capable sanity jobs complete successfully.

- VS Code Version: 1.132.0
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26100 (Windows 11 24H2)

## Installed extensions

- Anthropic — Claude Code for VS Code
- Gunders89 — Siemens SCL
- mechatroner — Rainbow CSV
- Microsoft — .NET Install Tool
- Microsoft — C#
- Microsoft — C# Dev Kit
- Microsoft — Pylance
- Microsoft — Python
- Microsoft — Python Debugger
- Microsoft — Python Environments
- tomoki1207 — vscode-pdf

Note on the "extensions disabled" answer: the MCP servers list is surfaced through Copilot Chat, so the visible UI symptom cannot be observed with all extensions disabled. However, the underlying HTTP 406 response is verifiable independent of any extension using curl (see reproduction steps below).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up an MCP server using `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore` v1.2.0 with `.WithHttpTransport(options => options.Stateless = true)`, or any spec-compliant MCP Streamable HTTP server.

2. Configure the server in `mcp.json`:

    ```json
    { "servers": { "test": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:PORT/" } } }
    ```

3. Open the MCP servers list in VS Code chat.

4. Observe the server shows a connection error such as:

    ```
    Error sending message to http://localhost:PORT/: TypeError: fetch failed
    ```

5. Reproduce the underlying HTTP 406 with curl (fails):

    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:PORT/ \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Accept: application/json" \
      -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0"}}}'
    ```

    Response: `HTTP 406 Not Acceptable`, body:

    ```json
    {"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream"}}
    ```

6. Verify it works with the correct Accept header (200 OK):

    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:PORT/ \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
      -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0"}}}'
    ```

## Root cause

Per MCP specification 2025-06-18, POST requests to a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint MUST include an `Accept` header listing both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`. The official `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore` SDK (v1.2.0) enforces this requirement strictly and returns HTTP 406 with the message above when the client's `Accept` header omits one of the two values.

The VS Code built-in MCP HTTP client appears to send an `Accept` header that does not include both values, triggering the 406 and surfacing as `TypeError: fetch failed` in the MCP servers list.

## A/B evidence from the same setup

Three local MCP servers, identical `mcp.json` config (`type: "http"`, only URL differs), same host:

| Server | Version | MCP spec | VS Code result |
|---|---|---|---|
| afry-sim-io | 0.3.1 | 2024-11-05 | Works |
| AfryOpcUaConnector | 2.3.0.0 | 2025-06-18 | Fails 406 → "fetch failed" |
| AfryTiaMcp | 3.5.8.0 | 2025-06-18 | Fails 406 → "fetch failed" |

The one server that works uses an older MCP spec version whose SDK does not enforce the strict Accept-header check. The two failing servers implement the current spec (2025-06-18) strictly.

## Cross-client confirmation

A second MCP client, Claude Code, connects successfully to all three servers using the exact same configuration (`type: "http"`, same URLs). It sends `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` per spec. This rules out any server-side or network-side issue.

## Server-side log, first-party evidence of client behavior

[2026-08-10 17:38:42.994] REQ  req-001 id:0 initialize
[2026-08-10 17:38:43.099] RES  req-001 id:0 initialize  ok   (109ms)

[2026-08-10 17:52:37.220] ERR  req-011 ?  error: [invalid JSON payload parse error]

Our MCP server has a logging middleware that captures request/response per JSON-RPC message. Below is an excerpt showing traffic during a Claude Code session (baseline) followed by VS Code's attempts:

Four observations:

1. Claude Code (req-001 through req-003) completes the full MCP handshake normally: `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list`. Clean three-message flow.

2. VS Code (req-004 onward) never completes the handshake even when `initialize` returns 200. No `notifications/initialized` is ever sent. No `tools/list`. Instead the client sends repeated `initialize` requests. This suggests the client rejects even the successful 200 responses for a separate reason.

3. VS Code additionally sends malformed JSON in some requests (parser errors like "invalid start of a property name"). This is a separate bug from the Accept-header issue — the client is either double-escaping JSON or sending body bytes with incorrect encoding on retry attempts.

4. Alternating OK/406 pattern with the same client-server pair rules out intermittent network. The client is trying multiple transport variants in sequence, some of which pass the Accept-header check by accident (e.g., when no Accept header is sent — server falls back permissively).

## Request

Please update the built-in MCP HTTP client to send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` on its POST requests to MCP endpoints, per the Streamable HTTP transport section of the MCP specification.

Reference: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports

## Impact

Any spec-compliant MCP server using `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore` v1.2.0+ — and likely any other SDK implementing MCP spec 2025-06-18 Streamable HTTP strictly — is unusable from VS Code. This blocks integration of .NET-based MCP servers built to the current specification.

- #302394 — Same client (Streamable HTTP), different HTTP header issue (cookies for ARR affinity)

title: [cherry-pick] agentHost: perf: stop repairing worktree roots while listing

labels.name: cherry-pick-artifact
labels.description: Auto-generated cherry-pick PR

body:
Cherry-pick of #329986 from `main`.

Fixes #329880

## What

`listSessions` ran a data migration that re-derived every session's repository root through `git worktree list --porcelain`, to repair roots persisted by builds older than #328375. On a large catalogue that spawned hundreds of Git processes and made the first listing take ~52s — and the Agents window renders nothing until it returns.

This deletes the list-time repair. The listing now uses the persisted `copilot.worktree.repositoryRoot` as-is for the session's project label.

## Why this is safe

`WorktreeIsolation._readWorktreeMetadata` already canonicalizes the persisted root and **writes it back**, and every host-side consumer reads through it: archived resume, worktree removal, archive cleanup, unarchive recreation, and `resolveWorktreeProject`. Within the host, the listing's project label was the only consumer that did not.

Opening a session therefore still heals it: `_withWorktreeProject` resolves the worktree project, which canonicalizes and re-persists the root. `listSessions` also overlays the live summary, so every later listing reports the healed value from two independent sources.

That read-path repair is retained and is now the single repair point — `worktreeIsolation.test.ts` still covers it.

## Tradeoff (not a free removal)

The heal is **deferred rather than immediate**: restore deliberately emits no `sessionAdded`, and the renderer ignores `project` on `sessionSummaryChanged`, so the corrected root reaches the UI on the next `listSessions` refresh — which is turn- or reload-driven rather than periodic.

Until a legacy session is first opened, its sidebar group is named after the linked checkout, and renderer surfaces that read `folders[0].root` ("New Session" on a workspace section, and the customization writes on a just-opened session) can target that checkout. Those surfaces derive a Git root from a *display* field and so never read through the repairing reader — a pre-existing defect this change makes easier to hit, which I'll file separately. The target was a checkout of the same repository when it was persisted, and session creation re-canonicalizes the root, so a new session is still filed under the primary checkout. The merge-into-parent command cannot reach it at all: its only menu is gated on `ContextKeyExpr.false()` and it registers no `f1` entry.

Also accepted: a root persisted without its branch (only reachable via a partial metadata write) used to be repaired by the listing and now never self-heals. The reader's JSDoc records that.

## Measurements

On an 804-session catalogue: **49** sessions carry a worktree root across **4** distinct roots, and **all 4 were already primary checkouts** — the migration re-verified correct data on every listing and repaired nothing.

The issue's "613 sessions with persisted worktree metadata" is the count *with* metadata, not the count *needing repair*.

## Testing

- Replaced the repair-only test with two tests: one asserting the listing performs **zero** worktree-root resolutions and leaves metadata untouched, one asserting a legacy root heals once the session is opened (driving the real `restoreSession` path, so it guards `_withWorktreeProject`).
- Both were verified to **fail** with the production change reverted (0 passing / 2 failing), and the heal test also fails against an injected early-return in `_withWorktreeProject`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: 17 errors, identical to the clean-`main` baseline (pre-existing Copilot SDK drift).
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/vs/platform/agentHost/**/*.test.js"`: 4481 passing.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitService.integrationTest.ts`: 42 passing.
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: 42 errors, all pre-existing baseline.

title: Gate the Agents window sign-in requirement behind the signed-out opt-in
body:
The Agents window can force a GitHub sign-in modal before showing any of its UI. That gate used to ask two questions — and only one of them can be answered in time.

- **The gate combined two inputs**: is the `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable` opt-in on, *and* does some session type currently report that it runs without GitHub?
- **The second input lands too late.** The local agent host advertises its agents at `AfterRestored`, long after the setup widget has decided — so the gate raced the very modal it was meant to suppress.
- **Every consumer paid for the race**, needing a lifetime-scoped subscription just to retire a dialog it had already raised.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before ["Before"]
    direction LR
    O1["opt-in"] --> W1["window gate"] --> S1["force sign-in?"]
    R1["provider readiness"] -. "lands at AfterRestored" .-> W1
  end

  subgraph after ["After"]
    direction LR
    O2["opt-in"] --> W2["window gate"] --> S2["force sign-in?"]
    R2["provider readiness"] --> P2["per-type gate"] --> S3["SignInRequired, per type"]
  end
```

- **Drop the second input.** The window gate now reads the opt-in alone. Whether a session type needs GitHub isn't fixed — it flips as Claude and Codex credentials appear and disappear — so it belongs in the per-type gate, which re-runs every time the picker opens, not in a window gate that decides once at startup and never revisits.
- **No behavior change while the opt-in is off**, which is the default and is today's mandatory-sign-in behavior. With it on, a signed-out user gets the window immediately.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

### Changes

- `observeUsableWithoutGitHub()` → `observeAllowSignedOutWhenUsable()`, no longer taking `ISessionsManagementService`. Both `SessionsSetUpWidget` and `TitleBarAccountWidget` lose that dependency.
- Extracted `shouldForceGitHubSignIn()` so the window gate is one named, unit-testable predicate rather than an inline negation.
- Renamed `IAccountTitleBarStateContext.usableWithoutGitHub` → `allowSignedOutWhenUsable`. It carries the opt-in now, not a usability fact. This touches two one-line call sites in `mobileTitlebarPart.ts`.
- `IDiscoveredConfigNudgeContext.usableWithoutGitHub` is deliberately **not** renamed — that one really is provider-derived (the agent found an existing native config). Keeping the names distinct is the point.
- Refreshed the comments in `sessionsSetUpService.ts` that still narrated per-type readiness, including an `is does not require` typo.

### The TODO this removes

`sessionsAuthGate.ts` carried a ~20-line TODO acknowledging that this gate duplicated a judgement the per-type gate already makes (`getSessionTypeAvailability()` → `SignInRequired`), that the two predicates could drift, and that they already disagreed over `chatEntitlementService.anonymous` — the pickers honour it, the window gate ignored it. Removing the second input removes the duplication, so the TODO goes with it.

### Files

|---|---|
| `src/vs/sessions/browser/sessionsAuthGate.ts` | +26/−47 |
| `src/vs/sessions/browser/sessionsSetUpService.ts` | +33/−42 |

- Hazardous air quality (AQI 300+ in Delhi/Kolkata winters)
- Unreliable power grids (frequent outages)
- Poor internet connectivity
- Extreme heat/UV exposure

Currently, VS Code provides zero awareness of these ambient conditions. Developers in these regions work under physical stress without any tooling support, leading to health issues and data loss.

### Proposed Solution
Add an optional **"Environment-Aware Workspace"** mode to VS Code:

1. **Air Quality Alert**: When system location (coarse, privacy-preserving) indicates AQI &gt 150, show a subtle status bar indicator:
   - 🟡 Yellow dot: AQI 151-200 (Unhealthy) -> "Take screen breaks every 20 min"
   - 🔴 Red dot: AQI 201-300 (Very Unhealthy) -> "Limit outdoor work, use air purifier"
   - 🟣 Purple dot: AQI 300+ (Hazardous) -> "Avoid prolonged exposure, work indoors"

2. **Power Grid Stability**: Detect battery/UPS status. If running on battery + location is in known outage-prone region:
   - Auto-enable aggressive auto-save (every 5 seconds)
   - Show warning: "Unstable power detected. Auto-save enabled."
   - Suggest enabling local history backup

3. **Internet Quality**: When connection drops/reconnects frequently:
   - Suggest enabling offline mode
   - Cache documentation locally

4. **All data is offline/cached** - no real-time API calls. Uses:
   - WHO Global Ambient Air Quality Database (cached monthly)
   - System battery/AC status (already available)
   - Network connectivity API (already available)

### Why This Matters
- India has the 2nd largest developer population globally
- Developer wellbeing is increasingly recognized as productivity factor
- Minimal engineering cost - reuses existing VS Code status bar + settings infrastructure
- Privacy-first: all environment data is coarse-grained and local

### Alternatives Considered
- Separate extension: Overkill for a core developer health feature
- OS-level notifications: Not contextual to coding workflow
- Third-party apps: Developers don't install separate wellness apps

### Additional Context
I am a developer from Kolkata, India, where winter AQI exceeds 300 and power outages are common during coding sessions. I would be happy to provide local AQI correlation data or participate in user studies.

title: agentHost: perf: stop repairing worktree roots while listing

labels.name: release-cherry-pick
labels.description: Automated cherry-pick between release and main branches

body:
Fixes #329880

## What

`listSessions` ran a data migration that re-derived every session's repository root through `git worktree list --porcelain`, to repair roots persisted by builds older than #328375. On a large catalogue that spawned hundreds of Git processes and made the first listing take ~52s — and the Agents window renders nothing until it returns.

This deletes the list-time repair. The listing now uses the persisted `copilot.worktree.repositoryRoot` as-is for the session's project label.

## Why this is safe

`WorktreeIsolation._readWorktreeMetadata` already canonicalizes the persisted root and **writes it back**, and every host-side consumer reads through it: archived resume, worktree removal, archive cleanup, unarchive recreation, and `resolveWorktreeProject`. Within the host, the listing's project label was the only consumer that did not.

Opening a session therefore still heals it: `_withWorktreeProject` resolves the worktree project, which canonicalizes and re-persists the root. `listSessions` also overlays the live summary, so every later listing reports the healed value from two independent sources.

That read-path repair is retained and is now the single repair point — `worktreeIsolation.test.ts` still covers it.

## Tradeoff (not a free removal)

The heal is **deferred rather than immediate**: restore deliberately emits no `sessionAdded`, and the renderer ignores `project` on `sessionSummaryChanged`, so the corrected root reaches the UI on the next `listSessions` refresh — which is turn- or reload-driven rather than periodic.

Until a legacy session is first opened, its sidebar group is named after the linked checkout, and renderer surfaces that read `folders[0].root` ("New Session" on a workspace section, and the customization writes on a just-opened session) can target that checkout. Those surfaces derive a Git root from a *display* field and so never read through the repairing reader — a pre-existing defect this change makes easier to hit, which I'll file separately. The target was a checkout of the same repository when it was persisted, and session creation re-canonicalizes the root, so a new session is still filed under the primary checkout. The merge-into-parent command cannot reach it at all: its only menu is gated on `ContextKeyExpr.false()` and it registers no `f1` entry.

Also accepted: a root persisted without its branch (only reachable via a partial metadata write) used to be repaired by the listing and now never self-heals. The reader's JSDoc records that.

## Measurements

On an 804-session catalogue: **49** sessions carry a worktree root across **4** distinct roots, and **all 4 were already primary checkouts** — the migration re-verified correct data on every listing and repaired nothing.

The issue's "613 sessions with persisted worktree metadata" is the count *with* metadata, not the count *needing repair*.

## Testing

- Replaced the repair-only test with two tests: one asserting the listing performs **zero** worktree-root resolutions and leaves metadata untouched, one asserting a legacy root heals once the session is opened (driving the real `restoreSession` path, so it guards `_withWorktreeProject`).
- Both were verified to **fail** with the production change reverted (0 passing / 2 failing), and the heal test also fails against an injected early-return in `_withWorktreeProject`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: 17 errors, identical to the clean-`main` baseline (pre-existing Copilot SDK drift).
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/vs/platform/agentHost/**/*.test.js"`: 4481 passing.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitService.integrationTest.ts`: 42 passing.
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: 42 errors, all pre-existing baseline.

body:
Steps to Reproduce:

1. restart a dev tunnel after it dies
2. try to connect

🐛 Failed to connect to tunnel 'aaron2-dx': [TunnelAgentHost] wait for forwarded port 31546 timed out after 30000ms

toggling remote access from the server off then on quickly can work around the issue by forcing a new tunnel to be created since the previous one is getting torn down.

```
2026-08-10 08:42:37.267 [info] Starting tunnel hosting...
2026-08-10 08:42:37.285 [info] Starting tunnel hosting as 'aaron1-dx'...
2026-08-10 08:42:37.774 [info] Adopted existing inactive tunnel: tidy-lake-5wpxgqm in cluster usw2
2026-08-10 08:42:38.871 [info] Tunnel relay host connected
2026-08-10 08:43:48.224 [info] Stopping tunnel hosting...
2026-08-10 08:43:48.227 [info] Stopping tunnel hosting...
2026-08-10 08:43:48.228 [info] Leaving adopted tunnel tidy-lake-5wpxgqm in place
2026-08-10 08:43:49.500 [info] Starting tunnel hosting...
2026-08-10 08:43:49.506 [info] Starting tunnel hosting as 'aaron1-dx'...
2026-08-10 08:43:50.003 [warning] Tunnel name 'aaron1-dx' is already in use by another active host; creating a new tunnel
2026-08-10 08:43:50.774 [info] Tunnel created: new-book-nwqwm6t in cluster usw2
2026-08-10 08:43:51.028 [info] Tunnel relay host connected
2026-08-10 08:44:11.019 [info] Incoming connection on port 31546, piping to local agent host
```

## some notes from copilot:

Yes. The timeout is now well isolated.

### What is working

For both `aaron1-dx` and `aaron2-dx`:

- Tunnel discovery succeeds.
- Control plane reports one connected host.
- Port `31546` is configured.
- Relay WebSocket connects.
- SSH negotiation and authentication complete.

### What fails

The live host never advertises port `31546`. A direct relay probe showed:

```text
connected
forwardedPorts: []
port events: []
```

So increasing the 30-second timeout will not help—the port never arrives.

### Likely cause

The tunnel record is stale or currently owned by an ordinary VS Code tunnel host, rather than the Agent Host sharing service.

The recent tunnel-adoption logic leaves adopted tunnels in place when sharing stops in `stopHosting`. That includes the Agent Host label and port metadata. If a regular tunnel host remains connected, the service reports:

- host online
- port configured

…but the live host does not actually forward that port. This also explains why auto-reconnect keeps retrying instead of treating it as offline.
